 THESE PETITIONS COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
In both these petitions, Petitioner is same.
He having died pendent lite, his L.Rs have been brought on record vide Court Order dated 14.2.2019.

In W.P.No.2851/2012, a challenge is laid to the Spl.
Deputy Commissioner's Order dated 7.1.2012 whereby, the granted land in question has been ordered to be restored to the original grantee under the provisions of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act, 1978.

entities.text: Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prohibition of Transfer of Certain Lands) Act, 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the companion case i.e., W.P.No.25202/2009, inter alia a direction has been sought for payment of compensation in respect of the subject land that has been since acquired u/s 28 of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966; other prayers have not been much pressed.

2. After service of notice, the State & its officials are represented by the learned AGA; the KIADB-SLAO is represented by the Sr. Panel Counsel; the private Respondents are represented by their own private counsel.
Learned advocates appearing for the respondents oppose the Writ Petition making submission in justification of the impugned order and repelling the petition prayers.
3. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and I have perused the Petition Papers.

The facts of W.P.No.2851/2012 are substantially similar to the one's treated by this Court in W.P.No.1776/2012 between SRI. KOTHANURU M THAMMANNA vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA &
OTHERS, disposed off vide judgment dated 13.02.2023.

entities.text:
SRI. KOTHANURU M THAMMANNA vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA &
OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The operative portion of the said judgment reads as under:
"In view of the above, this Writ Petition succeeds; a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned order of the 2nd Respondent- Deputy Commissioner (Annexure-A).

Consequently, KIADB is directed to release the compensation in favour of the Petitioners after ascertaining their credentials within a period of 8 weeks, failing which interest at the rate of 2% per month shall be payable on the amount due.

4. It hardly needs to be stated that in a given case, certain relief is granted to a litigant on the basis of foundational facts fitting in to the frame of law concerned, the courts have to accord the same relief to other litigants who are similarly circumstanced,
unless repugnant factors make such litigants a class apart for a differential treatment.
The relief in the litigant in the cognate case has been accorded on the basis of reasoning supplied in para 5 of the said judgment which reads as under:
B N Devaraj vs State Of Karnataka on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7769540/
6

entities.text: B N Devaraj vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Learned counsel for the petitioner is more than justified in banking upon the decision of the Apex Court in NEKKANTI RAMA LAKSHMI vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA & ANOTHER, 2018 (1) KAR L.R. 5 (SC) which is animated with the aforementioned long standing rule of law imbibed by all civilized jurisdictions.

entities.text: NEKKANTI RAMA LAKSHMI vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA & ANOTHER, 2018 (1) KAR L.R. 5 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is also force in the submission of learned counsel for the Petitioners that since the land is already acquired for the benefit of KIADB, the compensation is payable to his clients only.
He is right in saying that payment is interdicted by the interim orders of this Court and therefore, a direction be issued to release the compensation in favour of the Petitioners."

The very same fact matrix galoring from the record makes this case perfectly similar to the cognate one and therefore, the same reasoning avails for voiding the impugned order of the Spl. Deputy Commissioner.

5. In the companion case in W.P.No.25202/2009, the subject land having been acquired by the State for the benefit of the KIADB, the compensation has been paid to the private Respondents whose name figured in the property records as khatedars in the light of the Spl. Deputy Commissioner's order that is put in challenge in the other Writ Petition above.
Since the said order is being now voided in terms of the Apex Court decision reproduced supra, an order could have been made against the KIADB to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

However, the compensation having already been paid to the khatedars, a direction needs to be issued to them to - 10 - pay it back to the L.Rs of the Petitioner herein in a time bound way and with a reasonable rate of interest.
The reason for this is: the private Respondents having sold the property to the Petitioner by a registered instrument have received the price for that.
They have not offered to pay back the said amount when they secured the restoration order at the hands of the Spl. Deputy Commissioner.
They had used a socio welfare legislation i.e., 1978 Act as an instrument of fraud.
Such a conduct is unethical & unconscionable, to say the least and therefore, no leniency can be shown to such persons.

In the above circumstances, I make the following directions:
[i] W.P.No.25202/2009 succeeds with costs; a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned order dated 7.1.2022 made by the Spl. Deputy Commissioner whereby restoration of the subject land to the private Respondents herein was directed, and as a consequence, L.Rs of deceased Petitioner become the full owners of the subject land, ex post facto to the exclusion of the grantee or his L.Rs.
The private Respondents shall collectively pay to L.Rs of the Petitioner a sum of Rs.50,000/- as costs within eight weeks and delay will carry an interest at the rate of 2% per mensem.

sentences.text: [ii] W.P.No.2851/2012 is allowed; a Writ of Mandamus issues directing the KIADB to pay to L.Rs of deceased Petitioner the compensation in respect of the subject land acquired by accomplishing the award proceedings, if already not accomplished & payment is not made; however, if the payment received by the private Respondents, a direction issues to pay to the L.Rs of Petitioner the entire compensation with interest at the rate of 9% per annum reckoned from the date they had received it within three months, failing which, the delay would attract an addl. interest at the rate of 2% per mensem.

[iii] The private Respondents who have received the compensation, are hereby restrained from alienating or encumbering any of their private properties till the entire payment is made to the L.Rs of the Petitioner as directed above.
The jurisdictional authorities on the production of a copy of this order shall make an entry in respect of their private properties by way of endorsing the encumbrance immediately.

Deputy Commissioner whereby restoration of the subject land to the private Respondents herein was directed, and as a consequence, L.Rs of deceased Petitioner become the full owners of the subject land, ex post facto to the exclusion of the grantee or his L.Rs.
The private Respondents shall collectively pay to L.Rs of the Petitioner a sum of Rs.50,000/- as costs within eight weeks and delay will carry an interest at the rate of 2% per mensem.

7
[ii] W.P.No.2851/2012 is allowed; a Writ of Mandamus issues directing the KIADB to pay to L.Rs of deceased Petitioner the compensation in respect of the subject land acquired by accomplishing the award proceedings, if already not accomplished & payment is not made; however, if the payment received by the private Respondents, a direction issues to pay to the L.Rs of Petitioner the entire compensation with interest at the rate of 9% per annum reckoned from the date they had received it within three months, failing which, the delay would attract an addl. interest at the rate of 2% per mensem.
[iii] The private Respondents who have received the compensation, are hereby restrained from alienating or encumbering any of their private properties till the entire payment is made to the L.Rs of the Petitioner as directed above.
The jurisdictional authorities on the production of a copy of this order shall make an entry in respect of their private properties by way of endorsing the encumbrance immediately.
